cues.zh: 我们之前的所有图形操作都是基于像素网格定义的，这意味着顶点只能

cues.zh: 以这种方式移动。

cues.en: How do we solve this? Well if you know a little bit about graphics, you may be thinking of the word anti aliasing.
cues.zh: 怎么解决这个问题呢？如果你懂一点图形学，可能会想到“抗锯齿”（anti-aliasing）这个词。

cues.en: No, that's something else. Because look at this beautifully anti alias triangle that's still
cues.zh: 不，那是另一回事。因为你看这个抗锯齿效果极佳的三角形，它依然在

cues.en: jerking around
cues.zh: 一顿一顿地抖动，

cues.en: in an ugly fashion.
cues.zh: 看起来丑极了。

cues.en: What we actually want is something called sub pixel accuracy, which looks like this,
cues.zh: 我们真正想要的是所谓的子像素精度，看起来像这样，

cues.en: where even though it's alias, there's only black and white and there's jaggies,
cues.zh: 即使存在走样，只有黑白两色，还有锯齿，

cues.en: it's moving smoothly, and I can put the corners of the shape anywhere I want.
cues.zh: 它移动得很平滑，而且我能把形状的角点放在任意位置。

cues.en: How exactly does this work? Because it's not obvious anymore where exactly the edges on the pixel grid start or end,
cues.zh: 这到底是怎么工作的？因为像素网格上的边缘究竟从哪开始、到哪结束，已经不再明显了，

cues.en: when the pixel in the corner actually should be black, when it's partially covered, etcetera. And the key is something called sampling,
cues.zh: 角上的像素到底什么时候该是黑的，什么时候只是被部分覆盖，等等。关键是一种叫采样的方法，

cues.en: or using samples,
cues.zh: 或者说使用采样点，

cues.en: where whether a pixel is black or white is actually just defined by one thing, which is the point right in the middle. So if that point is inside the triangle, we color the
cues.zh: 一个像素是黑是白，其实只由一样东西决定，也就是正中间那个点。所以如果那个点在三角形内部，我们就给这个

cues.en: pixel black, otherwise we color it white.
cues.zh: 像素涂黑，否则涂白。

cues.en: And this might not seem like an important concept, but it really is because it defines everything that follows, and that's kind of why I'm talking about it first. Because what this means is there's really two worlds.
cues.zh: 这看起来可能不重要，但其实非常重要，因为它定义了后面的一切，这也是我先讲它的原因。因为这意味着其实有两个世界。

cues.en: On the left hand you have the world of vectors,
cues.zh: 左边是矢量的世界，

cues.en: where everything is mathematical and beautiful, your shapes are mathematically defined,
cues.zh: 那里一切都是数学的、优美的，你的形状由数学定义，

cues.en: and then you use sampling to transfer it over to the world on the right, which is the raster world, the world of pixels.
cues.zh: 然后用采样把它转换到右边的世界，也就是光栅世界、像素的世界。

cues.en: And you really have to think of this sort of as a final step.
cues.zh: 你真的得把这看作最后一步。

cues.en: And the reason is because when you actually look at this diagram,
cues.zh: 原因在于，当你实际看这张图时，

cues.en: on the left hand side those samples are in the middle of every pixel, and that means the edges of the pixel grid don't actually exist in vector world. They're sort of an artifact of the rasterization,
cues.zh: 在左边，那些采样点位于每个像素的正中间，这意味着像素网格的边缘在矢量世界里其实并不存在。它们算是光栅化的产物，

cues.en: if you will.
cues.zh: 如果你愿意这么说的话。

cues.en: And in fact we describe this as a nearest neighbor filter,
cues.zh: 事实上我们把这描述为最近邻插值滤波器，

cues.en: where when
cues.zh: 其中当

cues.en: we try to turn this grid of samples back into something continuous,
cues.zh: 我们尝试将这个采样网格重新转回连续的画面时，

cues.en: we just assign the color of the nearest sample to that area, and the fact that the pixels come out square is kind of just an artifact of
cues.zh: 我们只是把最近样本的颜色赋给该区域，而像素呈现出方形其实只是一种副产物，

cues.en: where the samples are placed.
cues.zh: 取决于样本的放置位置。

cues.en: And so this is ugly and pixelated.
cues.zh: 所以这看起来很丑且充满像素感。

cues.en: A better way is for example to use a bilinear filter,
cues.zh: 更好的方法是例如使用双线性插值滤波器，

cues.en: where you
cues.zh: 在这里你

cues.en: add gradients between pixels to sort of
cues.zh: 在像素之间添加渐变来使其

cues.en: even it out,
cues.zh: 变得平滑，

cues.en: and what's important about this diagram is that the color information is not again on the edges of the pixel grid, it's in the middle, and so the edges of the pixel are kind of a distraction, they don't factor in here.
cues.zh: 而这个图表重要的地方在于，颜色信息并不是在像素网格的边缘，而是在中间，所以像素的边缘其实是一种干扰，它们在这里并不起作用。

cues.en: So what actually is anti aliasing and aliasing
cues.zh: 那么抗锯齿和锯齿到底是用来

cues.zh: 其实就是这个。

cues.zh: 离远处越远，

cues.zh: 因为

cues.zh: 屏幕上单个像素的投影现在覆盖了远处非常、非常、非常广阔的区域。

cues.en: Looking at aliasing a bit closer
cues.zh: 更仔细地研究锯齿，

cues.en: has to do with something called the sampling theorem and the Nyquist frequency,
cues.zh: 就不得不提到一个叫做采样定理和奈奎斯特频率的概念，

cues.en: where if you take this pattern of bars
cues.zh: 如果你拿出这个条纹图案

cues.en: and you compress it, you get to this point where it goes white, black, white, black, white, black alternating,
cues.zh: 并对其进行压缩，你就会到达这样一个点：它变成白色、黑色、白色、黑色、白色、黑色交替，

cues.en: and you try to compress it further,
cues.zh: 而当你尝试进一步压缩它时，

cues.en: it starts to get messed up. In fact it folds in on itself and does something weird.
cues.zh: 它就开始出错。事实上它会折叠并产生一些诡异的现象。

cues.en: Running that backwards,
cues.zh: 反过来运行，

cues.en: you can see you approach the Nyquist frequency, white black white white white black, and then it expands smoothly again. So what that means is you can't compress
cues.zh: 你可以看到你接近了奈奎斯特频率，白黑白白白黑，然后它又平滑地展开了。所以这意味着你无法将

cues.en: any more variation onto the pixel grid than that particular
cues.zh: 比那个特定频率

cues.en: frequency,
cues.zh: 更多的变化

cues.en: because there's no room for it.
cues.zh: 压缩到像素网格上，

cues.en: And so the fact that you get jaggies when you're trying to draw shapes
cues.zh: 因为没有空间容纳它了。

cues.en: is really an artifact of aliasing,
cues.zh: 因此，当你试图绘制形状时出现锯齿，

cues.en: and instead of thinking again of the pixel edges, you need to look at the slopes here,
cues.zh: 实际上是走样产生的伪影，

cues.en: because of the pixel grid, there's a maximum slope between white and black that we can represent with this information,
cues.zh: 所以你不要再去想像素的边缘，而是需要看看这里的斜率，

cues.en: and that's really where the problem lies.
cues.zh: 因为像素网格的存在，白色和黑色之间存在我们用这些信息能够表示的最大斜率，

cues.en: It has very little to do with jaggies,
cues.zh: 而这才是问题所在。

cues.en: which is what most people think of when they talk about anti aliasing.
cues.zh: 这跟大多数人谈到抗锯齿时想到的锯齿关系不大。

cues.en: So what is anti aliasing?
cues.zh: 那么什么是抗锯齿？

cues.en: Is it blurring all the things?
cues.zh: 是把所有东西都模糊掉吗？

cues.zh: 算是吧。它是以一种特定方式进行模糊。你实际在做的是确定你的形状

cues.en: covers every pixel, and then shading the pixel proportionately.
cues.zh: 覆盖了多少像素，然后按比例给像素着色。

cues.en: And so you can do that mathematically using the rules of geometry to get an exact result,
cues.zh: 所以你可以利用几何规则通过数学方法做到这一点以获得精确的结果，

cues.en: but that's kind of annoying, especially when you have not one triangle, but let's say a million, which is not all that uncommon these days.

cues.en: So we use something else called super sampling,
cues.zh: 所以我们使用另一种叫做超采样的方法，

cues.en: where you put lots of samples inside the pixels,
cues.zh: 即在像素内部放入大量的采样点，

cues.en: and then you get in this case 16 shades of gray possible per pixel,

cues.zh: 你只需

cues.en: like your sample isn't just color,
cues.zh: 比如你的采样不只是颜色，

cues.en: it can have additional information associated with it. For example, depth. We use something called a Z buffer,
cues.zh: 它还可以关联额外信息。比如深度。我们使用一种叫 Z buffer 的东西，

cues.en: where for every pixel in your image you just record the depth as a number, in this case represented as a shade of grey,
cues.zh: 对于图像中的每个像素，你只需把深度记录为一个数字，这里用灰度深浅表示，

cues.en: and whenever you draw anything you update your depth map along with it, so that you know is the thing that I'm drawing
cues.zh: 每当你绘制任何东西时，都会同时更新深度图，这样你就知道我正在绘制的东西

cues.en: closer or further away than what's already there, So you can do per pixel cutting out of shapes that intersect without actually knowing
cues.zh: 比已有的东西更近还是更远，于是你可以逐像素裁掉相交的形状，而实际上不需要知道

cues.en: anything about the geometry involved. It's a sort of very dumb, but very effective way of doing it, and that turns out to be what GPUs are grayed out, because this is massively parallelizable.
cues.zh: 任何涉及的几何信息。这是一种很笨但非常有效的方法，而事实证明这正是 GPU 所擅长的，因为这件事可以大规模并行化。

cues.en: And aside from depth, for example, you might also record orientation in the form of normal, which is a vector, I'll go into that more later. For example, for something called deferred lighting,
cues.zh: 除了深度，比如你还可能用法线的形式记录朝向，它是一个向量，后面我会详细讲。比如，对于一种叫延迟光照的技术，

cues.en: where you generate an image like this,
cues.zh: 你会先生成这样一张图像，

cues.en: and then you paint the light in afterwards
cues.zh: 然后再把光照画上去

cues.en: using only this information.
cues.zh: 只使用这些信息。

cues.en: So you stop knowing
cues.zh: 于是你不再知道

cues.en: what is outside the frame of the picture, you don't even know what it represents, all you know is that you have a grid of samples with depth, normal, and color that you then use to do lighting with.
cues.zh: 画面画框之外是什么，你甚至不知道它代表什么，你只知道有一个采样网格，带有深度、法线和颜色，然后你用它们来做光照。

cues.en: So next step is the part where you learn linear algebra,
cues.zh: 所以下一步就是学线性代数的部分，

cues.en: and that might send
cues.zh: 这可能会让

cues.en: heart rates spiking a little bit,
cues.zh: 心率稍微飙升一下，

cues.en: but don't worry,
cues.zh: 但别担心，

cues.en: because we're going to do fun stuff with images.
cues.zh: 因为我们要用图像做一些好玩的东西。

cues.en: Let's start with something called the affine transforms, which you would know as the transform tool from Photoshop
cues.zh: 我们从所谓的仿射变换开始，你可能知道它是 Photoshop 里的变换工具

cues.en: or Illustrator,
cues.zh: 或 Illustrator 里的，

cues.en: and those transforms include
cues.zh: 这些变换包括

cues.en: rotation,
cues.zh: 旋转、

cues.en: scaling, and skewing,
cues.zh: 缩放和斜切，

cues.en: and they have something in common.
cues.zh: 它们有一个共同点。

cues.en: What they have in common is that they all preserve parallel lines no matter how you combine them, and that's a very useful property because it means you can describe the entire transform just by saying what it does to the grid.
cues.zh: 共同点是，无论你怎么组合，它们都会保持平行线，这非常有用，因为这意味着你只要说明它对网格做了什么，就能描述整个变换。

cues.en: So you
cues.zh: 所以你可以

cues.en: can describe the grid using something called a vector basis, which is just your X unit and Y unit, represented as an arrow in this case.
cues.zh: 用一个叫向量基的东西来描述网格，也就是你的 X 单位和 Y 单位，在这里用箭头表示。

cues.en: And because vectors are arrows, we can sort of do math with them,
cues.zh: 因为向量是箭头，我们可以对它们做点数学运算，

cues.en: and that's essentially linear algebra.
cues.zh: 这本质上就是线性代数。

cues.en: But let's forget about the numbers for a second and just do it on paper,
cues.zh: 不过我们先暂时忘掉数字，就在纸上做，

cues.en: and suppose for example that I define a new vector basis,
cues.zh: 假设我定义一个新的向量基，

cues.en: and I give you two arbitrary arrows and I say tell me what the smiley face looks like after it's been transformed,
cues.zh: 然后给你两个任意箭头，说告诉我笑脸图形变换后长什么样，

cues.en: or let's start with just that one point in purple, see what it looks like, or where it should be.
cues.zh: 或者先从那个紫色点开始，看看它变成什么样，或者说它应该在哪。

cues.en: And that's easy because you decompose it into its X and Y
cues.zh: 这很简单，因为把它分解成 X 和 Y

cues.en: coordinates, and then you reassemble it on the other side using the new grid.
cues.zh: 坐标，然后用新网格在另一边重新组装起来。

cues.en: And
cues.zh: 而

cues.en: because vectors are arrows, can also scale them, not just add them together, and that means that using this procedure of disassembling and reassembling, can find out where any point is
cues.zh: 因为向量是箭头，所以也能缩放，不只是相加；这意味着用这套拆解再重组的流程，就能找出任意点在哪里

cues.en: after it's been transformed
cues.zh: 在变换之后

cues.en: just by using your vector basis.
cues.zh: 只需用你的向量基。

cues.en: And
cues.zh: 而

cues.en: if you get this, then congratulations,
cues.zh: 如果你懂了这一点，那么恭喜，

cues.en: you get matrices,
cues.zh: 你就懂矩阵了，

cues.en: because these mysterious grids of numbers that they threw at you in school, and that they never really bothered to explain are really simple. They're the coordinates of the blue and the green dot that just describe where the grid has moved to when you're done transforming,
cues.zh: 因为学校里甩给你的那些神秘数字网格，他们从没认真解释过，其实特别简单；它们就是蓝点和绿点的坐标，描述你完成变换后网格移动到了哪里。

cues.en: and so the column on the left is just the X coordinate, Y coordinate of the blue points, the
cues.zh: 所以左边那一列就是蓝点的 X 坐标、Y 坐标，那个

cues.en: the green numbers are the x and y coordinate of the green point.
cues.zh: 绿色数字就是绿点的 x、y 坐标。

cues.en: The reason you put them in a matrix is because that allows you to do the computations effectively,
cues.zh: 把它们放进矩阵，是因为这样才能高效计算，

cues.en: in this case something called the matrix vector multiplication,
cues.zh: 在这个例子里，就是所谓的矩阵向量乘法，

cues.en: which is just transforming a point to conform to a new grid,
cues.zh: 也就是把一个点变换到新网格上，

cues.en: and it looks like this when you write it out.
cues.zh: 写出来是这样。

cues.en: And so again, you do this procedure of disassembling, in this case literally cleaving your matrix into two, and multiplying it by the two coordinates of the point that you're interested in, in this case transforming
cues.zh: 于是同样地，你执行这个拆解步骤，在这里就是字面意义上把矩阵拆成两部分，然后乘上你感兴趣的那个点的两个坐标，也就是在这个例子里

cues.en: the red point into the purple point,
cues.zh: 把红点变换成紫点，

cues.en: transforming a circle into an oval.
cues.zh: 把一个圆变换成椭圆。

cues.en: And then if we want to, for example, apply another transformation, let's say a rotation,
cues.zh: 然后如果我们想，比如说，应用另一个变换，比如旋转，

cues.en: we find that our vector basis has just moved to a new location,
cues.zh: 我们会发现我们的向量基移到了新的位置，

cues.en: which means there's just a new matrix.
cues.zh: 这意味着就有一个新的矩阵。

cues.en: And this is where matrix
cues.zh: 而这就是矩阵

cues.en: math gets really interesting,
cues.zh: 数学真正有趣的地方，

cues.en: because if you do the naive solution to this problem, you apply two transforms as in the bottom,
cues.zh: 因为如果你用最直白的解法，你就像下面那样应用两个变换，

cues.en: and
cues.zh: 而且

cues.en: you know for every transformation that you pile on you have to do another matrix multiplication.
cues.zh: 你知道每叠加一个变换你就得再做一次矩阵乘法。

cues.en: But because of the properties,
cues.zh: 但得益于这些性质，

cues.en: you can condense them all together,
cues.zh: 你可以把它们全部合并起来，

cues.en: and
cues.zh: 最终

cues.en: end up just optimizing in a way into a single transform.
cues.zh: 以某种方式优化成一个单一变换。

cues.en: And that's sort of the secret as to why computer graphics can be fast,
cues.zh: 而这正是计算机图形学能跑得快的秘诀，

cues.en: because you can condense the relationship and the placement of objects into just a single mathematical object of a constant size, namely a matrix.
cues.zh: 因为你可以把物体的关系和位置压缩成一个恒定大小的单一数学对象，也就是矩阵。

cues.en: And this works in two d, but it also works in three d. So a three d matrix is just a set of three vectors, in this case
cues.zh: 这在二维里成立，在三维里也同样成立。所以一个三维矩阵就是一组三个向量，在这个例子里

cues.en: red, green, blue, that define an orientation in space.
cues.zh: 红色、绿色、蓝色，它们定义了空间中的一个朝向。

cues.en: And in the matrix you end up with three columns of three coordinates,
cues.zh: 在矩阵里你最终得到三列、每列三个坐标，

cues.en: and
cues.zh: 然后

cues.en: again you do a matrix multiplication
cues.zh: 你再一次做矩阵乘法

cues.en: to transform, in this case the flat smiley face, into one that's positioned in three d.
cues.zh: 来变换，在这个例子里，把扁平的笑脸变换成一个定位在三维中的样子。

cues.en: And it also works in four dimensions,
cues.zh: 而且它在四维空间中也适用，

cues.en: and that can be a little weird.
cues.zh: 这可能会有点奇怪。

cues.en: Now,
cues.zh: 那么，

cues.en: why on earth would you do this, what's the point,
cues.zh: 到底为什么要这么做，意义何在，

cues.en: what is the fourth dimension?
cues.zh: 第四维是什么？

cues.en: Well the key is actually in the image, which is four dimensions projected back into three d, where suddenly parallel lines are no longer parallel.
cues.zh: 其实关键就在这张图里，它是把四维投影回三维，此时原本平行的线不再平行了。

cues.en: Which is interesting because that's what perspective does. And when you're rendering in three d, often you want perspective, you want it to look natural,
cues.zh: 这很有意思，因为透视就是这样产生的。当你在三维中渲染时，通常需要透视，希望看起来自然，

cues.en: and that is
cues.zh: 而这正是

cues.en: why we use four dimensions. And I can't really show you four dimensional math because picturing that is kind of kooky,
cues.zh: 我们使用四维的原因。我无法真正向你展示四维数学，因为想象那个有点烧脑，

cues.en: but I'll show you how it works for two dimensional images
cues.zh: 但我会展示它在二维图像中如何运作，

cues.en: where you apply the third dimension to do the same kind of trick. So the
cues.zh: 即应用第三维来做同样的把戏。所以，

cues.en: reason we use four dimensional matrices to do three d math is the same reason we use three-dimensional matrices to do two d math.
cues.zh: 我们用四维矩阵做三维数学的原因，和我们用三维矩阵做二维数学的原因是一样的。

cues.en: And it works like this, you have ordinary two dimensional space, a grid,
cues.zh: 它是这样运作的，你有普通的二维空间，一个网格，

cues.en: and you end up sort of doing a bat signal thing where you project it outward like this,
cues.zh: 然后你像蝙蝠信号那样把它向外投影，

cues.en: and you apply, so this is space, this is three d, and yet we call it two dimensional space, why? Well because the image that we're projecting is two dimensional, and just like a bat signal projected onto a cloud,
cues.zh: 然后应用，所以这是空间，这是三维，但我们称之为二维空间，为什么？因为我们投影的图像是二维的，就像投影在云上的蝙蝠信号，

cues.en: the light along any particular ray is constant,
cues.zh: 沿任意特定射线的光是恒定的，

cues.en: which means you only have two degrees of freedom instead of three.
cues.zh: 这意味着你只有两个自由度而不是三个。

cues.en: Why do we do this? Well because what happens when you start changing the vector basis?
cues.zh: 我们为什么要这么做？因为当你开始改变向量基的时候会发生什么？

cues.en: And
cues.zh: 还有

cues.en: in doing so, we've gained a couple new things. For one, we've gained a whole new Z vector, the red one,
cues.zh: 这样做下来，我们得到了几个新东西。首先，我们得到了一个全新的Z向量，就是红色的那个，

cues.en: which didn't exist before, we just made that up. And that's the interesting one, because if you move that one,
cues.zh: 这是以前不存在的，是我们编出来的。这个才有意思，因为如果你移动这一个，

cues.en: you aim the bat signal,
cues.zh: 你瞄准蝙蝠信号，

cues.en: just like that.
cues.zh: 就是这样。

cues.en: And that means that all of a sudden, instead of just being able to change shapes
cues.zh: 这意味着，突然之间，我们能做的不再只是改变形状

cues.en: in place,
cues.zh: 原地，

cues.en: we can move them around as well, which is something that affine transforms couldn't do on their own.
cues.zh: 我们也可以移动它们，这是仿射变换本身做不到的。

cues.en: So you get translation and scaling effects where if you pull out the red vector or push it in, of changing its length, you end up tightening the beam or expanding
cues.zh: 这样就能产生平移和缩放效果：把红色向量向外拉或向内推，改变它的长度，最终会让光束变窄或扩展。

cues.en: the beam.
cues.zh: 光束。

cues.en: And we have something else, is that our X and Y vectors now also have a Z coordinate,
cues.zh: 我们还有另外一点，就是我们的 X 和 Y 向量现在也有了一个 Z 坐标，

cues.en: which until now has just been zero, and they control the alignment of the image.
cues.zh: 这一项此前一直是零，它们控制图像的对齐方式。

cues.en: Because if I change those, for example tilting them all the way back, you see that you tilt the image so that part of it is now closer to the projection point,
cues.zh: 因为如果我改变它们，比如把它们全部向后倾斜，你会看到图像随之倾斜，使得其中一部分现在更靠近投影点，

cues.en: part of it is further away, which ends up being what perspective does. So if you project this back down to two dimensions,
cues.zh: 其中一部分更远，这正是透视的作用。所以如果把它投影回二维，

cues.en: now your parallel lines are no longer parallel,
cues.zh: 现在你的并行线条不再平行了，

cues.en: and you've
cues.zh: 而你

cues.en: done perspective transforms.
cues.zh: 已完成透视变换。

cues.en: And then that has an interesting
cues.zh: 然后这就带来了一个有趣的

cues.en: implication,
cues.zh: 蕴含，

cues.en: because it means that if I'm drawing something like this, a cube in three d space, I can position and move and orient it using a single four dimensional matrix.
cues.zh: 因为这意味着，如果要画这样一个三维空间里的立方体，只需一个四维矩阵，就能搞定它的定位、移动和朝向。

cues.en: And
cues.zh: And

cues.en: it has a structure where in the upper left portion there's a three by three normal matrix that
cues.zh: 它有一种结构，在左上角部分有一个三乘三的法线矩阵

cues.en: controls rotation, scaling, skewing.
cues.zh: 控制旋转、缩放、倾斜。

cues.en: There's one for translation,
cues.zh: 还有一个用于平移，

cues.en: which is shining the beam differently in four dimensional space. And then there's
cues.zh: 也就是在四维空间中以不同方式投射光束。然后还有

cues.en: Z, sorry, in this case the W coordinates, the fourth coordinate DHL,
cues.zh: Z，抱歉，在这个情况下是 W 坐标，第四个坐标 DHL，

cues.en: which
cues.zh: 它

cues.en: controls perspective and creates
cues.zh: 控制透视并产生

cues.en: narrowing lines effects and vanishing points and that sort of thing.
cues.zh: 线条收窄效果和消失点之类的效果。

cues.en: And
cues.zh: 而且

cues.en: like I said,
cues.zh: 就像我说的，

cues.en: matrices can be condensed. Applying five matrices in a row, you can express that as just one single combined matrix,
cues.zh: 矩阵可以合并。连续应用五个矩阵，你可以把它表示为一个单一的合并矩阵，

cues.en: which is very handy,
cues.zh: 这非常方便，

cues.en: and that means that the mathematical relationship between that little black cube on the screen,
cues.zh: 这意味着屏幕上那个小黑立方体之间的数学关系，

cues.en: and as it's defined in three d space,
cues.zh: 以及它在三维空间中定义的方式，

cues.en: and the actual location on the screen as it's projected
cues.zh: 和它在屏幕上投影的实际位置

cues.en: is defined by a single matrix, and I can show you how that works.
cues.zh: 是由一个单一矩阵定义的，我可以给你演示这是怎么运作的。

cues.en: We start in object space,
cues.zh: 我们从对象空间开始，

cues.en: which is what you're looking at, the cube on its own defined with the
cues.zh: 也就是你正在看的东西，立方体本身，其定义是

cues.en: origin sort of at its center of mass, or if it's a character usually you put it under their feet, but just somewhere in the middle so you have a point of reference.
cues.zh: 原点大致在其质心处，如果是角色的话通常会放在脚下，但总之放在中间某个位置，这样你就有一个参考点。

cues.en: You transform object space into world space
cues.zh: 你把对象空间变换到世界空间

cues.en: by placing objects
cues.zh: 通过放置物体

cues.en: with a matrix.
cues.zh: 用一个矩阵。

cues.en: You can scale them, rotate them, move them around, etcetera.
cues.zh: 你可以缩放它们、旋转它们、移动它们等等。

cues.en: And world space is where everything else lives, so in this case I added a camera and I added a ground plane so that it has something to sit on.
cues.zh: 而世界空间是其他一切所在的地方，所以在这个例子中我添加了一个相机，还添加了一个地平面，让它有东西可以放置在上面。

cues.en: And world space is again defined relative to some reference point,
cues.zh: 而世界空间同样是相对于某个参考点来定义的，

cues.en: which is the frame that you're doing all your placement
cues.zh: 也就是你进行所有摆放

cues.en: and simulation in.
cues.zh: 和模拟所用的坐标系。

cues.en: Then we have another matrix transformation that takes you to view space,
cues.zh: 然后我们还有另一个矩阵变换，把你带到视图空间，

cues.en: which is a coordinate system centered on your camera.
cues.zh: 这是一个以相机为中心的坐标系。

cues.en: In this case Z points forward,
cues.zh: 这里 Z 轴指向正前方，

cues.en: but that's a convention and you have to be careful which way your axis points when you're doing these things.
cues.zh: 但这只是一种约定，做这些事时你得注意坐标轴指向哪个方向。

cues.en: And finally from view space,
cues.zh: 最后从视图空间，

cues.en: we go
cues.zh: 我们进入

cues.en: into screen space, which is simply pixels and pixel units.
cues.zh: 屏幕空间，也就是简单的像素和像素单位。

cues.en: And so because
cues.zh: 所以因为

cues.en: we're doing matrix transformations,
cues.zh: 我们在做矩阵变换，

cues.en: this entire chain
cues.zh: 整个这条链

cues.en: ends up being implemented
cues.zh: 最终被实现

cues.en: or represented as a single transformation,
cues.zh: 或表示为一个单一的变换，

cues.en: and you can go backwards as well, but that's a little bit trickier.
cues.zh: 你也可以反向进行，但那会稍微棘手一些。

cues.en: Finally, I just want to talk about shaders, which is how these things are actually implemented
cues.zh: 最后，我只想谈谈着色器，这些实际上是如何实现的

cues.en: on graphics card.
cues.zh: 在显卡上。

cues.en: Say for example you have a three d model,
cues.zh: 比如你有一个三维模型，

cues.en: which in this case is defined
cues.zh: 在这个例子中它被定义

cues.en: as vertices,
cues.zh: 为顶点，

cues.en: points in space,
cues.zh: 空间中的点，

cues.en: and triangles that span those points. So in terms of data structure you're looking at a list of vectors which define points,
cues.zh: 以及跨越这些点的三角形。所以就数据结构而言，你看到的是一组定义点的向量，

cues.en: and then a set of indices saying triangle one goes from one to two to three, triangle two goes from two to three to four, etcetera, and that makes up this whole object in object space.
